## [0.7.5] - 2026-10-11

### Added

- The emergency CLI can now erase attendees' personal data when the admin UI and API are unreachable: `admitto attendees erase --event <id> --attendee-ids <id[,id...]> --operator-email <email>` (`--dry-run` only counts, `--yes` skips the question, up to 500 ids). It does what the erase API does, including audit entries (marked `source: "cli"`, ids and counts only), stored export and import files, and wallet passes at the provider; it exits with code 2 when a pass is still there, so running it again retries. `admitto attendees find --query "<name or email>" [--event <id>]` finds the ids (read-only, up to 20 people, erased people not listed, works on an archived event). The DSAR procedure now points to both instead of a manual SQL delete.
- Wallet passes of attendees whose personal data was erased are now also deleted at the wallet provider when the erasure itself could not do it (provider down, no wallet credentials yet, timeout): the worker's daily retention run and `admitto retention run` (`--dry-run` only counts) try again, event by event, and a run that runs out of its 60 seconds continues the next day. Passes that cannot be deleted are logged once per event and run (counts, failure codes, first attendee ids); an event with no wallet credentials raises the worker's retention line to a warning every day until it is dealt with.
- The worker's relay of log lines to the System logs no longer lets a burst push out the lines after it. The app takes 120 relayed lines a minute per address, and a provider that refused hundreds of calls in a row wrote a line for each, so the line that sums the burst up, and the summary of the run, were answered with 429 and never shown. The relay now sends at most 90 lines a minute, and at most 20 of any one message (the last of them says that more are held back); everything is still on the worker's own output.
- Files that attendee exports and imports leave in storage are now deleted: an export file 7 days after the export (`EXPORT_FILE_RETENTION_DAYS`) and the staged CSV of a finished import job 7 days after it finished (`IMPORT_STAGED_FILE_RETENTION_DAYS`), by the worker's daily retention run and `admitto retention run` (`--dry-run` only counts them). Erasing or removing an attendee deletes every export file of that event and the staged CSV of every finished import at once, and stops an export or import that is waiting or running (start it again, an import without that person). Deleting an event for good deletes the files its jobs left. A file that cannot be deleted is reported in the System logs and left to the retention run. Downloading an export whose file was just deleted now answers "not ready" instead of a server error.
- New staff API to remove an attendee from an event for good, with a reason from a fixed list (duplicate, test person, wrong import, added by mistake, other): `POST /api/admin/events/:eventId/attendees/:id/remove` and `POST …/attendees/bulk-remove`. It is for mistakes, so Reports change with it. Unlike the old delete it is refused on an archived event, leaves no name or address in the central audit log (reason, ids and counts only), blanks the address in saved import results and the creation audit entry, and deletes the wallet passes at the provider.
- Staff can now erase an attendee's personal data from the screens. **Erase personal data** is in the More actions menu of an attendee (their name has to be typed) and of the Attendees selection bar. The dialog says what is erased and what stays: the entry remains in Reports as an anonymous attendee, so totals do not change, but someone who had not checked in yet on a live event is cancelled and their place becomes free. An **Erased entries** switch in **Filters** lists erased people (muted, not selectable); the page of an erased attendee is read-only and shows **Erased** in place of everything personal. If a wallet pass could not be deleted at the provider, a dialog and the attendee's page offer **Try again**. Works on an archived event.
- The page of an erased attendee now says who erased the person, when and through what (admin or emergency command line), in a notice and in one **Activity log** entry. A Superadmin also sees the address the erasure was done from, because the central audit log it is read from is theirs alone; the staff API sends it to no one else. An erasure the log has no entry of keeps the old "History erased" line. The attendee detail response has a new `erasure` field.
- Staff can now remove an attendee from an event from the screens. **Remove from event** replaces **Delete attendee** and **Delete** in the More actions menus. It is for a mistake, a duplicate or a test person, so Reports change with it. The dialog asks for a reason (the choice is all that is saved about why) and the person's name for one attendee, and says when someone in the selection has already checked in. The Erase and Remove dialogs link to each other, so a wrong pick can be corrected. On an archived event it is off, with a tooltip pointing to **Erase personal data**. The Audit log tells an erasure from a removal and has one Action filter option for both.
- Wallet passes now leave out an attendee whose personal data has been erased: a pass being created while the erasure commits saves no install links and is deleted at the provider; updates, voiding, removal, pushes and wallet audiences skip the attendee. The last check before a pass update or push waits for an erasure that is still running. An Add to Wallet request running when the erasure commits is stopped at its last step and the visitor goes back to the ticket page (or gets the usual try-again notice if the check could not be made). What the provider already holds when the erasure commits still arrives.
- The staff API now treats an erased attendee as read-only: editing, resending, copying the ticket link, dismissing a bounce, notes, revoking a check-in or item, and every wallet action answer "attendee erased" (409), also when the erasure commits while the request runs. Bulk edits and bulk revokes skip erased attendees, and the Attendees list leaves them out unless asked (`include_erased=1`), reporting how many are hidden. Copying a ticket link and previewing a sent message wait for a running erasure and hand out nothing for someone being erased. Exports and the personal data export wait for a running erasure just before the file is built and leave that attendee out; the Overview activity feeds and revoke counts leave erased attendees out too.
- New staff API to erase an attendee's personal data (one attendee, or a selection): the name, email, company, notes, answers, ticket link and message copies are removed, the entry stays in Reports as an anonymous attendee, the wallet pass is deleted at the wallet provider (repeating the request retries a pass that could not be deleted) and the address is blanked in the saved results of imports. The audit log records who erased how many people and which ids, never their names. Works on an archived event.
- Groundwork for erasing an attendee's personal data without changing Reports: an attendee can be marked as erased, which keeps the row (ticket type, check-in, admission hour, wallet and mail counts) but replaces the name and email with placeholders and clears every other personal detail, note, activity entry, message copy and ticket link. A ticket can never be issued to an erased attendee again; the database refuses an erased row that still holds personal data and refuses to undo an erasure; no attendee can be given an address ending in `@erased.invalid`.
- Sending ticket emails now leaves out an erased attendee and waits for a running erasure instead of queueing a message with the old address and name. The last check before a message goes to the mailer (a retry, the worker, a synchronous send) waits too, also when staff addressed another attendee's message to that person's email. A message already in the mailer's hands when the erasure committed still goes out once and does not write its result back onto the emptied record. Bulk send audiences no longer include erased attendees.
- Check-in, undoing or revoking a check-in, handing out and taking back items, notes and the activity log now refuse an attendee whose personal data has been erased, and wait for an erasure that is still running instead of writing onto the emptied record. An erased attendee no longer shows in the door search, the recent check-ins list or the scan card.
- Automated PR review can request a Codex subscription review when Claude is unavailable and a scoped GitHub trigger token is configured. Actions approves only a verified clean Codex result for the current commit, links the result, and leaves findings unapproved.
- One loading standard for the staff app. A full-screen loading screen shows the Admitto mark and says what is loading, from the first frame; grey placeholders in the shape of what is coming (never a bare spinner) appear only if a read takes longer than a fraction of a second; "Taking longer than usual. Check your connection." shows after 8 seconds, and a read with no answer after 30 seconds ends in an error with a **Retry**. The spinner takes the colour of its button or text and turns visibly in Windows High Contrast mode. The rules are in `standards/admin-spa/loading.md`.
- The automated pull request review now keeps one status comment on the pull request, edited in place: which commit it reviewed, which model, turns, how much of the diff the reviewer actually saw, which tools it used, the run and the attempt budget, with a warning when it approved without seeing the whole diff. When a run fails, times out, hits the usage limit or is rejected by its login, the comment says why and what to do. The repository owner can comment `/ai-review` (review again), `/ai-review status` or `/ai-review cancel`. The model step is stopped after 15 minutes, and the reviewer's session is confined to Read, Grep and Glob inside the checkout, with no MCP tool or server. See `docs/dev/ai-review-how-it-works.md` and `docs/dev/ai-review-lessons.md`. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.

### Changed

- The "View" details popover of the Audit log and the Security audit log is now placed by the same positioning code as the other menus: it opens above the button when there is no room below, stays inside the window on narrow screens, and closes when the page scrolls. A new test fails when someone adds hand-written positioning for a floating panel instead of using the shared code.
- The date picker, the time picker, the timezone picker and the venue suggestions list now open in the same way as the menus and searchable selects: placed by the one shared positioning code instead of four separate copies. They no longer flash in the wrong place for a frame near the edge of the window, stay inside the window with a margin on narrow screens, open above the field when there is no room below, and keep their place while the page is zoomed or the phone keyboard is open. The date picker still moves to the field's right edge when it would not fit to the right.
- The automated pull request review now reads the `AGENTS.md` of the folders a change touches and every file that the root `AGENTS.md` names for that area (the `standards/` pages, the attendee erasure rules and so on), so the reviewer applies the same rules as a coding agent working there (the admin loading standard is no longer in the root file). Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- Any rate limit can now be retuned with the `RATE_LIMIT_OVERRIDES` environment variable (JSON keyed by limit name, for example `{"auth:login-ip":{"max":60}}`), without a new release or image. Recreate the container after changing it; an invalid entry is skipped with a warning at startup and the rest still applies. The check-in stream keeps its own `CHECKIN_STREAM_*` variables. See `deploy/ENV.md` and `docs/security/SECURITY-CONTROLS.md`.
- The per-address limits on sign-in, passkey sign-in and single sign-on are higher (30, 30 and 60 per minute, were 10, 10 and 20), so a group of staff signing in at the door from one venue Wi-Fi address no longer locks each other out. The per-account limits (sign-in per email, MFA, password re-check) are unchanged.
- The staff API no longer has `DELETE /api/admin/events/:eventId/attendees/:id` and `POST /api/admin/events/:eventId/attendees/bulk-delete` (they answer 404): the hard delete is now `POST …/attendees/:id/remove` and `POST …/attendees/bulk-remove`, which need a reason and are refused on an archived event, and a privacy request goes through the erase routes. Audit entries the old routes wrote before still hold the person's name and email in the central audit log; the retention SQL in `DATA-PROTECTION.md` blanks them.
- The automated pull request review now allows 100 attempts per pull request and 1000 per day (was 6 and 80), so a busy stack of pull requests keeps getting real reviews instead of a policy approval with no review. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- The loading spinner now takes the colour of the button or text around it instead of a fixed blue, so it is visible on primary buttons and follows the brand colour elsewhere, and skeleton placeholders use their own colour tokens.
- Every screen of the staff app now follows the shared loading standard (see Added): Attendees, Check-in, Account, Users & roles, Organisation settings, Event settings, Communication, Reports, the setup wizard, the New event dialog, Import, the event Overview, Requirements, the events picker and opening an event by its address. Buttons show their own spinner, keep their label and keyboard focus while they work and ignore a second click; **Retry** stays on screen, busy, with the focus until the answer is in; and anything that could not be loaded looks the same everywhere (a red cross, a title such as "Could not load users", the reason and a **Retry**).
- Operators now stay signed in automatically on the day of an event they are assigned to: no inactivity timeout, kept after closing the app, until 06:00 the next morning (or the event's end if later), however they sign in. Only a sign-in made that day counts. The **Keep me signed in** checkbox is gone. Administrators and superadmins are unaffected. A superadmin can turn this off with the **Operators stay signed in on event day** switch in Settings → Security (`operator_event_day_sessions` or `OPERATOR_EVENT_DAY_SESSIONS`, on by default), which replaces the 0.7.4 days setting and `OPERATOR_REMEMBER_ME_DAYS` (the old values are ignored). `remember_me` is no longer accepted at sign-in.

### Fixed

- One stored email message that can no longer be rendered no longer stops the mail queue. A delivery saved before the stricter template checks (for example a ticket link in an unquoted attribute) made the sending run throw before any mail went out, so every later run stopped on the same row. That row now fails on its own, for good, with the fixed error "The stored message can no longer be rendered." (also on retry, on a resend and in the delivery log preview, which shows no message instead of an error), and the other messages in the run are sent.
- Email retries and worker sends now share per-delivery ownership: concurrent attempts are skipped, cancelled/reclaimed snapshots and stale outcomes cannot replace the current revision, and retention preserves newly queued message bodies and in-flight retries while their provider outcomes are recorded.
- CSV and XLSX imports now preserve quoted multiline fields as one attendee record. Upload limits and diagnostic row numbers count non-empty data records; malformed CSV records receive a fixed validation error.
- Address search and map-pin lookup now use separate cache entries. Daily forecasts also keep each event time zone separate, so one event cannot reuse another time zone's temperature range.
- Docker Compose now gives the worker the same Redis credentials as the application and migration service, so a stale reference URL cannot leave background jobs using an old password. Preflight warnings and deployment guidance cover all three services.
- Invalid or out-of-range import recovery intervals now fall back to the default instead of producing an invalid database cutoff.
- Manual attendee creation, restoration and imports now share the final event-capacity lock, so concurrent operations cannot consume the same last place. Lock acquisition leaves a full work budget for waiting operations; a slow acquisition is retried only before writes begin. The standalone importer also checks capacity before committing; authorized force overrides remain available through the existing admin import flow.
- Undo check-in and new admissions now serialize the latest-entry decision per event and device, and undo checks the exact admission ID recorded by an earlier undo or revocation, so an overlapping or repeated undo cannot clear a newer admission or record a second reversal of the same one. Admin revocation locks admission state first and skips already reversed entries. Badge rollback and the audit stay in the same transaction.
- Chrome DevTools no longer reports "Incorrect use of <label for=FORM_ELEMENT>" on the Communication templates tab (the MJML/HTML body caption pointed at the editor's contenteditable, which is not a form field) or "A form field element should have an id or name attribute" on the attendee Notes tab, the Overview pinned note, the check-in note, and on any `Input` or `Select` without a visible label.
- The arrows on a scrolling tab strip (Event settings, Organisation settings) cover the clipped tab names again: the strip had grown 4px past its box for the focus ring, so a sliver of the first or last name showed beside each arrow.
- Menus and pickers (More actions, filters, searchable selects and the like) are now placed by the Floating UI library instead of our own measuring code. They no longer flash in the wrong place for a frame near the right edge of the window, stay inside the window with a margin on narrow screens and when zoomed, open above the button when there is not enough room below, and follow the button when their content changes size.
- A dialog that closes now fades away over 120ms instead of vanishing, and a notice that is in a dialog when it opens (the check-in notice of Remove from event) comes in with the dialog instead of sliding in by itself.
- Clicking outside a dialog that has fields to fill in (Add attendee, Create event, a template, an item, a note, an edit) no longer closes it and loses what was typed: Cancel or Escape close it. Confirmations and read-only views still close on a click outside, but not while their request runs.
- The reason in Remove from event is now a select like the other fields instead of five radio buttons, and the list of what Erase personal data takes and what stays says Erased and Stays once each instead of on every line.
- In Reports, the hourly chart grows to the height of the By ticket type list beside it instead of leaving an empty strip under the hour labels.
- The descriptions in the Danger zone are no longer cut at 640px, so they stay on one line where there is room, and the focus ring of a tab is no longer cut at the top. The text under the wallet preview has more space above it, and notices wrap like other running text.
- Descriptions and hints no longer wrap into short, even lines with a wide empty strip beside them (the "Remove this person from the event?" dialog, the Add item and Add custom field dialogs, the item drawer and the Danger zone): running text now runs to the edge of its column like ordinary text, and only headings, card titles, empty states, notices, toasts and tooltips keep even lines. "check-in" is also broken at its hyphen less often.
- Pages and dialogs now enter the same way everywhere: every page fades in over 150 milliseconds (Communication, Check-in, Reports and Event settings used to appear at once, unlike Overview, Attendees and Requirements), and a dialog fades in with its dimmed backdrop and its panel rises a few pixels instead of appearing in one frame.
- Buttons with a short name no longer reserve room for a busy text and a spinner: "Export log" was a third wider than its text. While such a button works the spinner covers its label, and the busy text is only read out to assistive technology.
- The table in the AI review status comment no longer starts with an empty bar: its two columns now have the headings Item and Detail. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- Text no longer wraps one word to a line or gets cut off. Short texts have even lines ("Taking longer than usual. Check your connection." no longer leaves its last word alone). On a phone the tiles of Overview, Users and Reports show their whole labels, a notice with a button puts the button under its message, the alert types in Organisation settings and the Account page are one block per type, the attendee page subtitle is no longer squeezed beside its buttons, the Users cards show a user's whole name and address, and the Webhook URL and payload format are one under the other. On a laptop the check-in time chip of an attendee moves under the day when too narrow, the Users tiles no longer cut "1 of 2 local accounts enrolled", and the Active sessions table no longer breaks "Internal network" in the middle of a word.
- On a phone, the Activity log of the attendee page no longer squeezes its text into a column of one or two words (a row such as "Note added" took two lines and "Item issued" three, because the time and the person beside it left the text about 66 pixels), because the time and the person now go under the text of the row, and a note in the Notes tab no longer pushes its time past the edge of the card (only "09 0" of it showed): the author, the role and the time wrap onto the next line when they do not fit.
- The Active sessions table in Users & roles is easier to read on a laptop. From 1181 to 1499 pixels it now hides only its Sign-in column, where it used to show all eight columns from 1181 pixels and squeezed the login time, the signer's local time and the address into three to five lines (a row was up to 117 pixels tall at 1280 pixels, and from about 1360 pixels it is a line or two, about 60 pixels). Device and IP address stay, as they are what a person reviewing sessions looks at; the sign-in method is still on the cards, in the Staff users tab and on screens 1500 pixels wide and up.
- On the check-in page, when the counts and recent scans could not be loaded and **Retry** worked, the keyboard focus used to fall to the page, so a hardware scanner (it types like a keyboard) had nowhere to type and its next scan went nowhere until the operator clicked the scan field. The focus now goes to the scan field, and in the phone camera view to the list of recent scans.
- The Communication page of an archived event now shows the preview of its email templates. On both the Email and the Templates tab the preview was refused with the error "This event is archived." and stayed empty. A preview only shows a draft with sample data and saves nothing, so it now works on an archived event, while saving, sending and test emails stay blocked.
- The MJML or HTML body of an archived event's template can now be searched. You still cannot type into it, but you can click into it, select and copy text, and press Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on a Mac) to open the editor's own search, which also finds text below the part you can see. Before, you could not click into the editor at all, so the shortcut went to the browser's find, which only sees the lines the editor shows on screen.
- The hint "This event is archived. Editing is disabled." on the Subject and body fields of a template now appears right next to the field, like the one on **Send test**, instead of above the field's label.
- The Events list no longer repeats itself when every event is archived: "No active events" is followed by one short line on how to restore an event, and the extra **View archived events** button is gone because the **Archived events** tab is right above it.
- On an archived event, **Count recipients** on the Email tab is now off like **Send** (with the same hint) instead of failing with "This event is archived." when you click it, and **Resend** and **Dismiss bounce** in the delivery log do the same.
- On an archived event, the placeholder chips and the MJML or HTML switch above a template are now off, so a click can no longer change the read-only body and mark the template as having unsaved changes.
- The Overview and Reports pages of an archived event no longer try to open the live check-in feed, which the server refuses (the browser used to ask for it several times and get a "forbidden" answer each time), and no longer show the pulsing **Live** badge, since nothing there is live.
- Automated PR review now grants an explicit policy approval when Claude is unavailable or the automatic review budget is exhausted, stating that no AI review ran and the maintainer must review the diff manually before merging. Internal errors and incomplete diffs still receive no approval; Codex subscription fallback is deferred.
- Finishing the setup wizard or saving an operator's device label no longer resets the whole app: the session is refreshed in place instead of replacing every open page with a loading screen and dropping what was on it.
- Wallet confirm dialogs, notices, hover hints and report descriptions are now short enough to read before deciding: the two densest confirm dialogs (**Void every active wallet pass**, **Remove inactive wallet passes**) drop from a paragraph plus four bullet points to one or two short sentences, and the same applies across the other wallet dialogs and the Wallets report. Reversibility and how an action differs from a similarly destructive one are still stated.
- Event Settings → Danger zone's warning notice under the panel no longer sits about twice as far below it as the notices and cards elsewhere in Event Settings. It now uses the same standard gap.
- The **Void every active wallet pass** and **Refresh the wallet status** confirmation dialogs on Attendees now lead with one short sentence and list the rest as bullet points, matching the neighbouring **Remove inactive wallet passes** dialog, instead of one dense paragraph.
- Event Settings → Wallet's **API key** field no longer shows its **Change**/**Clear** links in full colour, looking clickable, once the event is archived. They were already disabled (archiving an event makes it read-only), this only fixes how they look.
- Event Settings → Wallet's **Pass expiration** control is now a single on/off switch, matching the Apple/Google/Samsung Wallet switches right above it, instead of two radio buttons, and its locked/not-ready notice no longer sits flush against the row above it.
- Event Settings → Wallet's **Field mapping** section now shows only one notice at a time, the empty-mapping hint before any field is added or the Semantic Tags hint once one is, instead of stacking both.
- Attendees → **More actions** → **Remove inactive passes** has a shorter, single-sentence hint.
- The Wallets report's **Pass validity** card description is now one short sentence instead of two dense ones.
- Health check rows now look the same before and after they are expanded: one font, size and line height, the icon, label and arrow aligned with the status circle, and the expanded text under the label. Degraded, Down and Not configured rows no longer repeat their state in a badge. The worker's **Last seen** age is a row in the expanded details, and the guidance under a problem row is split into labelled **What it affects** and **What to do** lines.
- The Health check tab now says why a problem happened: guidance under a down or degraded row starts with a **Why** line, ahead of **What it affects** and **What to do**. Rows that had no advice (data encryption, a slow Redis, an unsupported or unknown file storage provider) now have it, and a state Admitto does not recognise says so and suggests reloading and running the live checks again. When the core checks cannot be read at all, the Database, Rate-limit storage, Data encryption and Instance URL rows say "Could not evaluate ..." instead of showing an invented outage. **Wallet passes** no longer expands to an empty panel: it lists the events with Wallet on, set up and not set up yet.
- Attendees → **More actions** → **Remove inactive passes** used to report "There were no wallet passes ready to remove" the same way whether nothing was voided or expired at all, or some passes were but had not yet sat inactive for their required 24 hours - both looked exactly like the action had done nothing. The message now says how many are still within that 24-hour window when that is the reason, and the Wallets report's **Provider state** card shows the same count at any time, without having to run the action first.
- On a slow connection the icons, such as the Apple and Google Wallet marks in the Attendees list, no longer show as empty boxes until the icon font has loaded: they stay invisible and appear together, instead of the Samsung mark (an image) appearing alone first.
- Choosing an event on the check-in entry screen no longer flashes "No events with check-in access were found for your account" for a moment before opening check-in when you have access to exactly one event.
- The check-in search field is no longer offered an email address by the Bitwarden browser extension. Bitwarden now ignores a page's own "ignore this field" marking unless its user turns on "Allow websites to exclude fields to autofill", so the field's name now says it is a search box, which Bitwarden skips on its own.
- A Retry in a dialog that fails again with the same message is now announced again by screen readers, so it is clear that Retry did something (the Add attendee dialog's ticket types and custom fields), and when the control that has keyboard focus disappears from a dialog, such as that Retry once it worked, focus now moves to the first control in the dialog instead of falling to the page behind it, where the next Tab could leave the dialog, and a button that was switched off while it worked gets the focus back once it is on again.
- A button that is busy (Save, Send, Export, Retry and the rows in More actions) no longer takes keyboard focus away from the person who pressed it: it used to be switched off, which made the browser drop the focus onto the page, so after Enter the next Tab started from the top and the button was not selected again when the work ended. It now stays selected and ignores further presses until it is done.
- The loading spinner, including the one inside a busy button (Save, Send, Export, Retry), now shows that it is turning in Windows High Contrast (forced colours) mode: its bright head and its faint track were drawn in the same colour there, so the ring looked like a still circle and nothing showed that the page was working. It is now drawn there as a turning arc in the system's text colour, without the track (two system colours for head and track were tried, but nothing guarantees they differ enough from each other).
- Saving something on the Account page (profile, password, a two-factor change, revoking a session) no longer replaces the whole page with a loading screen while it refreshes: the page and whatever you have open or half-filled stays where it is, and a refresh that fails keeps the page and shows a warning with a **Retry** instead of an error. While the sessions list refreshes after a revoke, it and the account cards cannot be clicked, so the same session cannot be revoked twice. A profile you have just saved stays saved even if the refresh fails, an untouched field takes the new value when the page refreshes (what you typed is kept), and an older answer can no longer replace a newer one.
- A screen that could not load (the "Could not load …" screens with a Retry, and the shorter error lines in Account, Users, Sessions, Security, Import, System logs, the notification bell and the identity editors) is now announced the same way by a screen reader, as an alert, as soon as it appears. Before, some were only a polite status and some were not announced at all. The look is unchanged.
- The list of events on the start screen now has a **Retry** button when it fails to load, like every other screen that could not load (it only showed the error before).
- Three more warnings that a screen reader could miss are now announced as alerts: "Someone else updated this attendee" after a save is refused, "Live updates stopped coming through" above the Audit, Security and System logs, and the "Something went wrong" screen. **Retry now** in the logs warning is a small button that shows it is working, and in System logs the warning goes away as soon as **Retry now** gets an answer.
- On Attendees, a ticket-type, custom-field or item list that failed to load is now announced by a screen reader as soon as the page opens (before, the message only existed inside the **Filters** panel). **Retry** in that panel, in the Communication and Wallets send panels and in the attendee edit dialog no longer disappears when pressed, which dropped keyboard focus onto the page: the message and button stay, the button shows it is working, and a repeated failure is announced again.
- The thin progress bar that shows a page change, or a list or card being refreshed, is now visible in Windows High Contrast (forced colours) mode. The bar is a plain coloured background, which that mode redraws in the colour of the page, so it could not be seen and only the dimming of a refreshed card showed that something was loading. It now draws in the system's text colour, which that mode guarantees to stand out from the page, also while it finishes and when reduced motion holds it still.
- **Previous** and **Next** under a list with pages (Attendees, notes and activity log, the audit, security and delivery logs, sessions, Reports) no longer take keyboard focus away: they used to switch off on the first or last page and while a page loaded, so the browser dropped the focus onto the page. They now still look switched off but stay selected, show the usual focus outline and do nothing when pressed.
- On an Organisation settings tab that could not load (General, Mail, External services, Notifications, Security) and on the mail card of Event settings, keyboard focus no longer falls onto the page behind when **Retry** works: the error and the **Retry** button that had focus go away together, so a screen reader lost its place and the next Tab started from the top of the page. Focus now moves to the tab's own panel, which a screen reader announces by name, and the next Tab goes to its first field. Focus that has already moved elsewhere is left alone.
- If saving the cropped logo fails after **Apply changes** (the organisation logo in Branding or in the setup wizard, or the event logo in Event settings), the reason now appears inside the crop window, where you are looking. Before, it was written on the page behind the window, so **Apply changes** just stopped spinning with no message and you could press it again without knowing why. You can press it again or choose **Cancel**.
- Removing a logo, or a logo whose preview turns out broken, while a new file is still going up no longer leaves the logo area stuck as busy. Before, once the server had answered, **Replace image** and the file picker stayed off, and in Organisation settings, Branding, **Save** and **Reset to saved** stayed off until the page was reloaded. The late answer is still thrown away.
- Two ticket sends that overlapped (for example two staff members sending to the same attendees at the same time) could email an attendee a second copy of their ticket: a ticket that finished sending while the second send was still working through its recipients was mistaken for one sent earlier, so it went out again as a resend. Whether an attendee already had a ticket is now read once, when a send starts. A ticket that finishes in the meantime is skipped as already sent, and sending again to someone who got their ticket before the send started still resends it, as before.
- The topbar **System status** no longer says "All systems normal" before it knows. For a superadmin it now says "Checking systems…" with a neutral dot while the health checks are read, and a failure that is already known is shown at once. With an event open, the Email sending row waits for that event's own mail settings too. If the checks do not answer within 30 seconds, they show as Unavailable with a **Check again** item in the menu, and the event's row falls back to the organization's status.

### Security

- The check-in screen's POST requests (scan, lookup, admit, item, note, undo) now refuse a body larger than 32 KiB with `413 request too large`, and the worker's log relay to `/api/ops/system-logs` one larger than 64 KiB. The check is made before the body is parsed, after the session or token, the same-site check and the rate limit have already answered, so an unauthorized request still gets its 401 or 403 and no body is read for it. Ordinary requests are far below the limits: the largest real field is a note of at most 2,000 characters.
- The weather providers' replies (Open-Meteo and MET Norway) are now read with a 1 MB limit, counted on the bytes as they arrive, so a provider that sends an oversized or never-ending body can no longer fill the app's memory; the forecast is then shown as unavailable, like any other provider failure. Real replies are a few KB (Open-Meteo) to well under 200 KB (MET Norway). `GEOCODING_TIMEOUT_MS` is now documented as the limit of one request to the geocoding service, counted from when the request starts: the one-request-per-second queue in front of it is not part of it.
- Custom email templates now preserve quoted HTML attribute context when an attribute contains literal angle brackets, so attendee values containing quotes remain data instead of creating another attribute.
- Import upload and queue logs now use identifiers, counts and safe file metadata without recording uploaded filenames; authorized import history keeps the filename.
- Production browser error reports now contain only a fixed error category. Exception text, names, stacks and page URLs stay out of server and System logs; the server independently rejects arbitrary diagnostic fields. Local development diagnostics remain detailed.
- Wallet provider failures now use fixed error messages and safe log categories, so reflected names, email addresses and barcode credentials do not enter routine logs. Retry, duplicate recovery and pass-removal behavior are preserved.
- Import and export failures now store fixed, privacy-safe messages instead of upstream exception text. Job status and import history also hide unknown errors saved earlier, while preserving capacity, erasure and worker-recovery messages.
- Erasing or removing an attendee now immediately makes earlier exports of that event unavailable, even when deleting their stored files fails. File cleanup remains retryable, and a new export made after the change can still be downloaded.
- Adding a passkey, a security key or an authenticator app to an account that already has a second-factor method now asks to confirm with a code from an existing method, a backup code, or an existing passkey. Before, anyone holding a signed-in session (for example a stolen session cookie) could attach their own second factor to the account without proving anything. The account's first method needs no confirmation. The API takes the proof in a new `step_up` field on `POST /api/account/mfa/totp/confirm` and `POST /api/account/mfa/webauthn/register/finish`.
- "Remember this device" can no longer be set by a session that did not itself pass two-factor sign-in a moment ago. Before, any signed-in session (for example one using a stolen session cookie, or one that came from single sign-on or a passkey sign-in) could mark a browser as trusted and skip two-factor on later password sign-ins. The offer after a passkey check still works and now records an audit entry like the checkbox does. Removing an authenticator app or a passkey now also forgets every remembered device on the account. Sessions get a new `mfa_verified_at` column (additive migration; existing sessions simply cannot remember a device until they sign in again).
- "Remember this device" can no longer outlast a "forget all devices" (or password change, or removal of a sign-in method) that happens at the same moment. Before, a request that had just passed its two-factor check could still save a new trusted device after the revocation had run, leaving a cookie that skips two-factor. The check and the save now happen under one lock, and the revocation takes the same lock first.
- TOTP secrets and identity provider client secrets are now encrypted bound to their purpose (AES-GCM additional data), so a stored ciphertext copied into another encrypted column no longer decrypts. Existing values keep working and are upgraded the next time they are saved. After a value is saved by this version, an older build cannot read it, so do not roll back across this change without re-entering those secrets.
- Stored mail credentials (SMTP password, Microsoft Graph client secret, Power Automate key and URL), event wallet API keys, the bounce-mailbox IMAP password and the notification webhook URL are now encrypted bound to their own purpose, like TOTP and identity provider secrets, so a ciphertext copied into another column no longer decrypts. Existing values keep working and are upgraded when saved again; administrators can upgrade all at once with `npm run db:rebind-secret-contexts` (`-- --dry-run` to preview; Docker installs: `node packages/db/dist/scripts/rebind-secret-contexts.js [--dry-run]`, see `deploy/README.md`). Upgraded values cannot be read by an older release, so do not roll back after running it.
- Bounce ingest no longer lets anyone who can mail the bounce mailbox mark an attendee's message as bounced. For messages sent over SMTP, a delivery bounces only when the returned notice names the Message-ID Admitto recorded at send time; notices that do not are counted as having no matching delivery. Messages sent through Microsoft Graph or Power Automate have no such id and still match by recipient. If your SMTP relay rewrites the Message-ID, bounces for those messages are no longer applied.
- Outbound destinations (OIDC discovery, mail transports, notification webhooks, Open-Meteo and Nominatim URLs) now also reject carrier-grade NAT space (100.64.0.0/10, which includes Alibaba Cloud's metadata endpoint), multicast, reserved and benchmarking ranges, all of 0.0.0.0/8, and IPv4 addresses hidden in NAT64, 6to4 or IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals. A service reached over Tailscale (100.x.y.z) is blocked too: for an identity provider or mail server add its exact host to `SSO_PRIVATE_DESTINATION_ALLOWLIST` or `MAIL_PRIVATE_DESTINATION_ALLOWLIST`.
- Creating a named event image now validates the optional pre-crop original path the same way the event logo does, so only a branding upload path or an http(s) address is stored; anything else is rejected with `invalid_original_url`.
- Admin and superadmin sessions now end after 12 hours at most, as the documentation always said. A migration had stored 7 days as the setting on every instance, so the 12 hour default in the code was never used. A data migration moves a stored value of exactly 7 days to 12 hours; any other value in Settings → Security is kept, so an instance that chose 7 days on purpose has to set it again. People already signed in keep their original end time.
- Two more buttons no longer lose keyboard focus while they work: **Mark all as read** / **Clear all** in the notification bell and **Undo last check-in** in the mobile check-in overlay now stay selected, show they are busy and ignore further presses. When the focused button in a menu goes away, focus moves to the next button in the menu. **Retry** in the notification list and the Bounce detection card stays on screen, busy and with focus, until the answer arrives.
- Guessing a sign-in code is now limited per account, not only per session and per address: someone who knows an administrator's password could previously open a new sign-in, and so a new set of guesses, every few tries, from a different IPv6 address each time. The limit now counts all attempts on the account, and every IPv6 address inside one /64 network counts as one client for the sign-in, setup, single sign-on and two-factor limits.
- The per-email limit on sign-in attempts now applies before the password is checked: after too many attempts for one address even the correct password is refused until the minute has passed, so the limit slows down guessing instead of only the wrong guesses.
- Changing your own password now also signs out every device you had marked as trusted for two-factor sign-in, so a trusted device set up before the change cannot skip the code afterwards.
- Sign-in, setup, two-factor code entry and the wallet provider's webhooks now refuse oversized requests (over 16 KB, or 64 KB for webhooks) before reading them, so a single huge request from the internet can no longer exhaust the server's memory.
- A decompression-bomb `.xlsx` import can no longer exhaust the server's memory by lying about the size of its contents: the real size is measured while unpacking, with the existing limits, and the file is refused when it is over them.
- A wallet provider webhook sent to one event's address can no longer change the registration counts or timestamps of another event's pass by naming that pass only by its identifier.
- Signed wallet provider deliveries are now limited per event only after their signature has verified. Before, anyone who knew an event's (public) id could send junk to its webhook address and use up its allowance, so the provider's real deliveries (void and registration signals) were refused for that event; unauthenticated requests are now limited per source address only.
- A live check-in or overview feed now closes when its permission ends instead of only being checked when it was opened: within about 25 seconds of the session being revoked or expiring, the account being disabled, the person losing access to the event, or the event being archived, the feed stops, so a closed tab left open no longer keeps receiving attendee names.
- Replacing an event's wallet provider API key now takes effect for incoming webhook deliveries at once; before, the previous account's signing key kept being trusted (and the new account's genuine deliveries refused) until the server was restarted.
- The client address behind a reverse proxy is now the rightmost `X-Forwarded-For` entry that is not one of the proxies listed in `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`, instead of the first entry. A client can no longer choose its own rate-limit bucket by sending a forged `X-Forwarded-For` through a proxy that appends instead of overwriting. Setups where the proxy sets a single address are unchanged; with several proxies in a chain, list each of them in `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`.

---

### Deploy
- Container image: `ghcr.io/solarssk/admitto:0.7.5` (rolling `:0.7`)
- Migrations apply **automatically on container start**. **No manual `migrate deploy`.** Back up the database yourself before upgrading (the stack no longer takes an automatic pre-migration backup).

[Full changelog](https://github.com/solarssk/admitto/blob/v0.7.5/CHANGELOG.md)
